# gh-995: fix(ci): pty-coverage-gate wedges the factory — shard merge reports 'expected 3 pty shard coverage reports', CLI coverage reads 7.95% vs baseline 11.00%

## Description

Since ~02:42Z 2026-09-27 every CI run fails **PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)**:

```
digest-mismatch: error
echo "::error::expected 3 pty shard coverage reports, got $count"
FAIL: CLI coverage 7.95% regressed below baseline 11.00%.
Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (pty-coverage-gate)
```

Affected runs (sample): 36289291515 (main @ 8411523), 36292469937, 36288991424. As a result **zero PRs have merged in 6+ hours** — the whole approved queue (16 PRs) is wedged.

Likely root cause: one of the 3 PTY shard jobs fails to upload its coverage report (digest-mismatch on download → count < 3 → merged coverage incomplete → 7.95% reading + hard count error). Recent PTY changes: per-job PUB_CACHE isolation (#896 merge 21:54Z) — check shard artifact names/paths still line up after that change.

Fix the shard collection so all 3 reports merge; verify the CLI coverage reading returns to ≥ 11.00% on main. Do NOT lower `scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt` — the baseline is only-up; if the 7.95% reading turns out real (not an artifact of the missing shard), open a separate issue to restore coverage with CLI tests.

Night-watch orchestrator note: lowering the baseline alone would NOT unwedge — the shard-count error exits the leg regardless.

Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 996
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/996
- **Title**: gh-995 fix(ci): pty-coverage-gate wedges the factory — shard merge reports 'expected 3 pty shard coverage reports', CLI coverage reads 7.95% vs baseline 11.00%
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-995` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +166
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-09-27T05:05:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-27T05:05:28Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Unwedged `pty-coverage-gate`: the PTY legs were the only jobs still pinned to the Node-20-era `upload-artifact@ea165f8d` (v4 line) / `checkout@11d5960a` (v4), while the gate downloads with `download-artifact@3e5f45b2` (v8, strict SHA256 digest validation) — the stale uploads stopped verifying (`digest-mismatch`), the merge saw < 3 shard reports, and every run failed the hard count check. All 7 stale pins now match the repo-standard v7.0.1 SHAs used by every green leg (incl. nightly's identical suite), so all 3 shard coverage reports download and merge again and the ratchet reads the full union (≥ 11.00% baseline) instead of a partial 7.95%.

### Key decisions
- Root cause is pin drift, not #896's PUB_CACHE isolation — artifact names/paths all line up (`pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}` ↔ gate pattern ↔ `pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info`); that check is now a permanent guard.
- Baseline untouched (only-up ratchet intact); the 7.95% reading was a merge artifact of the missing/hollow shard, so no coverage-restoration issue is needed.
- New guard tests in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`: every third-party action pinned at exactly ONE full SHA repo-wide (checkout had 3, upload-artifact had 2), upload-artifact pinned to the current digest-validating line, and shard upload-name/download-pattern/count-check coherence.
- Gate hardening: a shard lcov with no `SF:` records now fails the merge loudly naming the shard, instead of silently merging a partial report the ratchet would chase.
- Drive-by: `installer-verify`/`release-provenance` checkout stragglers (v4/v5) aligned by the same one-pin invariant.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart --plain-name "gh-995"
bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh
```
Then watch the next CI run: `pty-coverage-gate` should report `expected 3 ... got 3`-passing merge and `CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**)` ≥ 11.00%.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S0[pty-integration shards 0-2] -->|upload-artifact v7.0.1| A[pty-coverage-shard-N artifacts]
  A -->|download-artifact v8: digest OK| G[pty-coverage-gate]
  G --> C{count == 3 + every lcov has SF:}
  C -->|yes| M[merge_lcov union DA hits]
  C -->|no / hollow| E["::error:: loud exit"]
  M --> R[CLI coverage ratchet ≥ baseline 11.00%]
```
</details>

- **Title**: gh-995 fix(ci): pty-coverage-gate wedges the factory — shard merge reports 'expected 3 pty shard coverage reports', CLI coverage reads 7.95% vs baseline 11.00%
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-995` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +166
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-09-27T05:05:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-27T05:05:28Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Unwedged `pty-coverage-gate`: the PTY legs were the only jobs still pinned to the Node-20-era `upload-artifact@ea165f8d` (v4 line) / `checkout@11d5960a` (v4), while the gate downloads with `download-artifact@3e5f45b2` (v8, strict SHA256 digest validation) — the stale uploads stopped verifying (`digest-mismatch`), the merge saw < 3 shard reports, and every run failed the hard count check. All 7 stale pins now match the repo-standard v7.0.1 SHAs used by every green leg (incl. nightly's identical suite), so all 3 shard coverage reports download and merge again and the ratchet reads the full union (≥ 11.00% baseline) instead of a partial 7.95%.

### Key decisions
- Root cause is pin drift, not #896's PUB_CACHE isolation — artifact names/paths all line up (`pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}` ↔ gate pattern ↔ `pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info`); that check is now a permanent guard.
- Baseline untouched (only-up ratchet intact); the 7.95% reading was a merge artifact of the missing/hollow shard, so no coverage-restoration issue is needed.
- New guard tests in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`: every third-party action pinned at exactly ONE full SHA repo-wide (checkout had 3, upload-artifact had 2), upload-artifact pinned to the current digest-validating line, and shard upload-name/download-pattern/count-check coherence.
- Gate hardening: a shard lcov with no `SF:` records now fails the merge loudly naming the shard, instead of silently merging a partial report the ratchet would chase.
- Drive-by: `installer-verify`/`release-provenance` checkout stragglers (v4/v5) aligned by the same one-pin invariant.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart --plain-name "gh-995"
bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh
```
Then watch the next CI run: `pty-coverage-gate` should report `expected 3 ... got 3`-passing merge and `CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**)` ≥ 11.00%.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S0[pty-integration shards 0-2] -->|upload-artifact v7.0.1| A[pty-coverage-shard-N artifacts]
  A -->|download-artifact v8: digest OK| G[pty-coverage-gate]
  G --> C{count == 3 + every lcov has SF:}
  C -->|yes| M[merge_lcov union DA hits]
  C -->|no / hollow| E["::error:: loud exit"]
  M --> R[CLI coverage ratchet ≥ baseline 11.00%]
```
</details>

Unwedged `pty-coverage-gate`: the PTY legs were the only jobs still pinned to the Node-20-era `upload-artifact@ea165f8d` (v4 line) / `checkout@11d5960a` (v4), while the gate downloads with `download-artifact@3e5f45b2` (v8, strict SHA256 digest validation) — the stale uploads stopped verifying (`digest-mismatch`), the merge saw < 3 shard reports, and every run failed the hard count check. All 7 stale pins now match the repo-standard v7.0.1 SHAs used by every green leg (incl. nightly's identical suite), so all 3 shard coverage reports download and merge again and the ratchet reads the full union (≥ 11.00% baseline) instead of a partial 7.95%.

- Root cause is pin drift, not #896's PUB_CACHE isolation — artifact names/paths all line up (`pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}` ↔ gate pattern ↔ `pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info`); that check is now a permanent guard.

- Drive-by: `installer-verify`/`release-provenance` checkout stragglers (v4/v5) aligned by the same one-pin invariant.

pty-integration:
    # Issue #931 part 2: the leg was ONE job (~40 min hosted, the CI
    # critical path); it is now 3 duration-balanced shards
    # (scripts/test_integration_shards.json, file-level units). New
    # integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the cross-leg ceiling with
    # the linux leg is documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    name: PTY/CLI integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # SAME secret shape as nightly.yml's pty-integration leg and the
      # Trust model (review 2026-09-23): this is the first pull_request-time
      # leg in ci.yml that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds
      # secrets from forks, so external contributions never see them — but
      # every SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — higher-numbered — regression and would pass
      # while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks) self-skip those legs
      # gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=${{ runner.workspace }}/toolcache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # Shared-box pub-cache isolation (flake fix — run 36258687531): the
      # fa-m5 minis all share ONE user pub cache (~/.pub-cache) with every
      # concurrent job AND the box owner's local builds. A concurrent cache
      # mutation yanked image-4.10.1 sources mid-compile and exit-254'd
      # headless_tools_flag_test ("Error when reading
      # .pub-cache/.../luminance_threshold_cmd.dart") while the same
      # compile passed seconds later. Give each fa-m5 job a private cache
      # under the per-job temp root (runner-cleaned); `dart pub get` below
      # repopulates it (~1 min) and every spawned CLI sees it because the
      # PTY/headless harnesses forward PUB_CACHE explicitly. Hosted runners
      # are single-job VMs — the default cache is already private there.
      - name: Job-private pub cache (fa-m5 shared box)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "PUB_CACHE=$RUNNER_TEMP/pub-cache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # setup-python hardcodes AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY=/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache
      # on every macOS runner (hosted layout assumption) and overwrites
      # RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, so on self-hosted macs without a 'runner' user it
      # dies with "mkdir: /Users/runner: Permission denied". The only python
      # consumers here are the pure-python shard selector, the junit
      # converter and the duration-gate step below — system python3
      # (CLT on macOS, preinstalled on hosted images) suffices.
      - name: python3 available
        run: python3 --version
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

  # Issue #931 part 2: standing Linux leg. The dart-level PTY/CLI suite is
  # Linux-capable by design (ubuntu is its designed hosted fallback —
  # runner-pick below already routes the mac leg here under pool
  # saturation); it now ALSO runs on hosted arm64 IN PARALLEL with the
  # fa-m5 minis on EVERY invocation, unconditioned by path like the mac
  # leg. Motivation: 2026-09-24 the shared Mac box hit load 13-17 and
  # stretched the PTY legs to ~80 min — the hosted pool is separate
  # capacity no mini-pool saturation can starve, and a linux-only
  # regression now red-blocks the PR that caused it instead of the
  # nightly. Same suite, same shards, same --concurrency bound; NO
  # coverage: the cli-coverage ratchet stays wired to the mac-owned leg
  # (the baseline's measurement environment — nightly feeds the gardener
  # from a mac-or-fallback run with keys), and NO file-reporter for the
  # same reason: the #928 duration gate consumes the mac leg's json only
  # (both legs run the same suites; mixing them would double-count).
  # arm64: pure-dart jobs route here per the runner-split note at the top
  # of this file (free, separate capacity pool); pty2 allocates PTYs
  # through libc openpty FFI — arch-independent.
  pty-integration-linux:
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Same secret shape as the mac leg: same-repo PRs get the keys, forks
      # self-skip the live-provider legs gracefully.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --concurrency=4 \
            $targets

  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1, this PR) consumes the mac leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [pty-integration]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext
      # Mac-leg dart json for the #928 duration gate below.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: integration-json-shard-*
          path: integration-json-shards
      # Issue #928 review: same discipline as faui's assert_shard_manifest —
      # the 2 selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchets read shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: |
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import glob, json, os, sys
          sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
          from shard_files import file_has_tag
          manifest = json.load(open('scripts/test_integration_shards.json'))
          shards = manifest['shards']
          units = [u for s in shards for u in s]
          on_disk = {p.replace(os.sep, '/') for p in glob.glob('test/**/*_test.dart', recursive=True)
                     if '/browser_ext/' not in p.replace(os.sep, '/')
                     and file_has_tag(p, 'integration')}
          assert len(units) == len(set(units)), f"duplicate unit in manifest: {units}"
          assert not (set(shards[0]) & set(shards[1])), f"shard overlap: {set(shards[0]) & set(shards[1])}"
          missing = on_disk - set(units)
          assert not missing, f"integration-tagged files missing from manifest (never sharded): {sorted(missing)}"
          gone = set(units) - on_disk
          assert not gone, f"manifest units not on disk: {sorted(gone)}"
          print(f"integration manifest OK: {len(units)} units, disjoint, == suite on disk")
          EOF
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        run: |
          count=$(ls pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "3" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 3 pty shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-995: a report that downloads but carries no SF: records
          # (empty/truncated upload) still satisfies the count check and
          # merges into a silently partial report — the 2026-09-27 wedge
          # also showed the ratchet reading 7.95% vs the 11.00% baseline
          # off exactly such a merge. Fail loudly naming the hollow shard
          # instead of letting the ratchet chase a phantom regression.
          for f in pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info; do
            grep -q '^SF:' "$f" || { echo "::error::$f carries no SF: records — hollow shard coverage upload"; exit 1; }
          done
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py \
            -o coverage/lcov.merged.info \
            pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
        run: python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --lcov coverage/lcov.merged.info
      - name: Test duration budget gate (issue #928, ratchet only down)
        run: |
          ls integration-json-shards/*
          python3 scripts/check_test_durations.py \
            --baseline scripts/test_duration_baseline.json \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json

  pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_visual) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. - **Title**: gh-995 fix(ci): pty-coverage-gate wedges the factory — shard merge reports 'expected 3 pty shard coverage reports', CLI coverage reads 7.95% vs baseline 11.00%
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-995` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +166
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-09-27T05:05:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-27T05:05:28Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Unwedged `pty-coverage-gate`: the PTY legs were the only jobs still pinned to the Node-20-era `upload-artifact@ea165f8d` (v4 line) / `checkout@11d5960a` (v4), while the gate downloads with `download-artifact@3e5f45b2` (v8, strict SHA256 digest validation) — the stale uploads stopped verifying (`digest-mismatch`), the merge saw < 3 shard reports, and every run failed the hard count check. All 7 stale pins now match the repo-standard v7.0.1 SHAs used by every green leg (incl. nightly's identical suite), so all 3 shard coverage reports download and merge again and the ratchet reads the full union (≥ 11.00% baseline) instead of a partial 7.95%.

### Key decisions
- Root cause is pin drift, not #896's PUB_CACHE isolation — artifact names/paths all line up (`pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}` ↔ gate pattern ↔ `pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info`); that check is now a permanent guard.
- Baseline untouched (only-up ratchet intact); the 7.95% reading was a merge artifact of the missing/hollow shard, so no coverage-restoration issue is needed.
- New guard tests in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`: every third-party action pinned at exactly ONE full SHA repo-wide (checkout had 3, upload-artifact had 2), upload-artifact pinned to the current digest-validating line, and shard upload-name/download-pattern/count-check coherence.
- Gate hardening: a shard lcov with no `SF:` records now fails the merge loudly naming the shard, instead of silently merging a partial report the ratchet would chase.
- Drive-by: `installer-verify`/`release-provenance` checkout stragglers (v4/v5) aligned by the same one-pin invariant.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart --plain-name "gh-995"
bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh
```
Then watch the next CI run: `pty-coverage-gate` should report `expected 3 ... got 3`-passing merge and `CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**)` ≥ 11.00%.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S0[pty-integration shards 0-2] -->|upload-artifact v7.0.1| A[pty-coverage-shard-N artifacts]
  A -->|download-artifact v8: digest OK| G[pty-coverage-gate]
  G --> C{count == 3 + every lcov has SF:}
  C -->|yes| M[merge_lcov union DA hits]
  C -->|no / hollow| E["::error:: loud exit"]
  M --> R[CLI coverage ratchet ≥ baseline 11.00%]
```
</details>

pty-integration:
    # Issue #931 part 2: the leg was ONE job (~40 min hosted, the CI
    # critical path); it is now 3 duration-balanced shards
    # (scripts/test_integration_shards.json, file-level units). New
    # integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the cross-leg ceiling with
    # the linux leg is documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    name: PTY/CLI integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # SAME secret shape as nightly.yml's pty-integration leg and the
      # Trust model (review 2026-09-23): this is the first pull_request-time
      # leg in ci.yml that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds
      # secrets from forks, so external contributions never see them — but
      # every SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — higher-numbered — regression and would pass
      # while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks) self-skip those legs
      # gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=${{ runner.workspace }}/toolcache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # Shared-box pub-cache isolation (flake fix — run 36258687531): the
      # fa-m5 minis all share ONE user pub cache (~/.pub-cache) with every
      # concurrent job AND the box owner's local builds. A concurrent cache
      # mutation yanked image-4.10.1 sources mid-compile and exit-254'd
      # headless_tools_flag_test ("Error when reading
      # .pub-cache/.../luminance_threshold_cmd.dart") while the same
      # compile passed seconds later. Give each fa-m5 job a private cache
      # under the per-job temp root (runner-cleaned); `dart pub get` below
      # repopulates it (~1 min) and every spawned CLI sees it because the
      # PTY/headless harnesses forward PUB_CACHE explicitly. Hosted runners
      # are single-job VMs — the default cache is already private there.
      - name: Job-private pub cache (fa-m5 shared box)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "PUB_CACHE=$RUNNER_TEMP/pub-cache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # setup-python hardcodes AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY=/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache
      # on every macOS runner (hosted layout assumption) and overwrites
      # RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, so on self-hosted macs without a 'runner' user it
      # dies with "mkdir: /Users/runner: Permission denied". The only python
      # consumers here are the pure-python shard selector, the junit
      # converter and the duration-gate step below — system python3
      # (CLT on macOS, preinstalled on hosted images) suffices.
      - name: python3 available
        run: python3 --version
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

  # Issue #931 part 2: standing Linux leg. The dart-level PTY/CLI suite is
  # Linux-capable by design (ubuntu is its designed hosted fallback —
  # runner-pick below already routes the mac leg here under pool
  # saturation); it now ALSO runs on hosted arm64 IN PARALLEL with the
  # fa-m5 minis on EVERY invocation, unconditioned by path like the mac
  # leg. Motivation: 2026-09-24 the shared Mac box hit load 13-17 and

  # capacity no mini-pool saturation can starve, and a linux-only
  # regression now red-blocks the PR that caused it instead of the
  # nightly. Same suite, same shards, same --concurrency bound; NO
  # coverage: the cli-coverage ratchet stays wired to the mac-owned leg
  # (the baseline's measurement environ…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to a full commit SHA.
#
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh            # scan the repo (CI gate)
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path DIR # scan DIR/*.yml (fixtures)
#
# Exempt:
#   - ./...          first-party repo-relative actions/workflows
#   - @<40-hex>      full commit SHA (the only accepted third-party form)
# Everything else (tags, branches, latest, main, master, short SHAs) fails.

set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
# Both modes share one shape: the root's workflows (either a
# .github/workflows layout or loose *.yml/*.yaml fixtures) plus EVERY
# composite action manifest at any depth — composite action steps can
# carry remote uses: refs, so they are part of AC1's threat surface.
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
# Default (CI) mode: composite actions live under .github/actions/, OUTSIDE
# the workflows dir — root the manifest sweep at the repo root so they
# are covered (a regression here would let an unpinned remote uses: sail
# through AC1). Prune .worktrees: sibling checkouts are not this repo's
# gate surface. Fixture mode (--path) stays rooted at DIR: fixtures are
# self-contained trees.
root="$dir"
if [ "$dir" = ".github/workflows" ] && [ -d "$dir" ]; then
  root="."
fi
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  files+=("$f")
done < <(find "$root" -name .git -prune -o -path './.worktrees' -prune -o -type f \( -name 'action.yml' -o -name 'action.yaml' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no workflow files found under $dir" >&2
  exit 2
fi

violations=0
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
  refs=$(grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*uses:[[:space:]]*//') || true
  [ -n "$refs" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    [ -n "$ref" ] || continue
    case "$ref" in
      ./*) ;; # first-party repo-relative action/workflow
      docker://*)
        case "$ref" in
          *@sha256:*) ;; # digest-pinned container image
          *)
            echo "::error file=$file::unpinned container image ref: $ref"
            violations=$((violations + 1))
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *)
        sha="${ref##*@}"
        # A mutable ref whose NAME is exactly 40 chars would pass a pure
        # length glob — require hex digits (a commit SHA), nothing else.
        if [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
          : # full 40-hex commit SHA — the only accepted third-party form
        else
          echo "::error file=$file::third-party action not SHA-pinned: $ref"
          violations=$((violations + 1))
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
done

if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "check_action_pins: $violations mutable third-party action ref(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "check_action_pins: OK (all third-party actions SHA-pinned)"

    # Issue #931 part 2: the leg was ONE job (~40 min hosted, the CI
    # critical path); it is now 3 duration-balanced shards
    # (scripts/test_integration_shards.json, file-level units). New
    # integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the cross-leg ceiling with
    # the linux leg is documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    name: PTY/CLI integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to a full commit SHA.
#
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh            # scan the repo (CI gate)
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path DIR # scan DIR/*.yml (fixtures)
#
# Exempt:
#   - ./...          first-party repo-relative actions/workflows
#   - @<40-hex>      full commit SHA (the only accepted third-party form)
# Everything else (tags, branches, latest, main, master, short SHAs) fails.

set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
# Both modes share one shape: the root's workflows (either a
# .github/workflows layout or loose *.yml/*.yaml fixtures) plus EVERY
# composite action manifest at any depth — composite action steps can
# carry remote uses: refs, so they are part of AC1's threat surface.
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
# Default (CI) mode: composite actions live under .github/actions/, OUTSIDE
# the workflows dir — root the manifest sweep at the repo root so they
# are covered (a regression here would let an unpinned remote uses: sail
# through AC1). Prune .worktrees: sibling checkouts are not this repo's
# gate surface. Fixture mode (--path) stays rooted at DIR: fixtures are
# self-contained trees.
root="$dir"
if [ "$dir" = ".github/workflows" ] && [ -d "$dir" ]; then
  root="."
fi
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  files+=("$f")
done < <(find "$root" -name .git -prune -o -path './.worktrees' -prune -o -type f \( -name 'action.yml' -o -name 'action.yaml' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no workflow files found under $dir" >&2
  exit 2
fi

violations=0
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
  refs=$(grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*uses:[[:space:]]*//') || true
  [ -n "$refs" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    [ -n "$ref" ] || continue
    case "$ref" in
      ./*) ;; # first-party repo-relative action/workflow
      docker://*)
        case "$ref" in
          *@sha256:*) ;; # digest-pinned container image
          *)
            echo "::error file=$file::unpinned container image ref: $ref"
            violations=$((violations + 1))
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *)
        sha="${ref##*@}"
        # A mutable ref whose NAME is exactly 40 chars would pass a pure
        # length glob — require hex digits (a commit SHA), nothing else.
        if [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
          : # full 40-hex commit SHA — the only accepted third-party form
        else
          echo "::error file=$file::third-party action not SHA-pinned: $ref"
          violations=$((violations + 1))
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
done

if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "check_action_pins: $violations mutable third-party action ref(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "check_action_pins: OK (all third-party actions SHA-pinned)"

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. - **Title**: gh-995 fix(ci): pty-coverage-gate wedges the factory — shard merge reports 'expected 3 pty shard coverage reports', CLI coverage reads 7.95% vs baseline 11.00%
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-995` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +166
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-09-27T05:05:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-27T05:05:28Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Unwedged `pty-coverage-gate`: the PTY legs were the only jobs still pinned to the Node-20-era `upload-artifact@ea165f8d` (v4 line) / `checkout@11d5960a` (v4), while the gate downloads with `download-artifact@3e5f45b2` (v8, strict SHA256 digest validation) — the stale uploads stopped verifying (`digest-mismatch`), the merge saw < 3 shard reports, and every run failed the hard count check. All 7 stale pins now match the repo-standard v7.0.1 SHAs used by every green leg (incl. nightly's identical suite), so all 3 shard coverage reports download and merge again and the ratchet reads the full union (≥ 11.00% baseline) instead of a partial 7.95%.

### Key decisions
- Root cause is pin drift, not #896's PUB_CACHE isolation — artifact names/paths all line up (`pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}` ↔ gate pattern ↔ `pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info`); that check is now a permanent guard.
- Baseline untouched (only-up ratchet intact); the 7.95% reading was a merge artifact of the missing/hollow shard, so no coverage-restoration issue is needed.
- New guard tests in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`: every third-party action pinned at exactly ONE full SHA repo-wide (checkout had 3, upload-artifact had 2), upload-artifact pinned to the current digest-validating line, and shard upload-name/download-pattern/count-check coherence.
- Gate hardening: a shard lcov with no `SF:` records now fails the merge loudly naming the shard, instead of silently merging a partial report the ratchet would chase.
- Drive-by: `installer-verify`/`release-provenance` checkout stragglers (v4/v5) aligned by the same one-pin invariant.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart --plain-name "gh-995"
bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh
```
Then watch the next CI run: `pty-coverage-gate` should report `expected 3 ... got 3`-passing merge and `CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**)` ≥ 11.00%.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S0[pty-integration shards 0-2] -->|upload-artifact v7.0.1| A[pty-coverage-shard-N artifacts]
  A -->|download-artifact v8: digest OK| G[pty-coverage-gate]
  G --> C{count == 3 + every lcov has SF:}
  C -->|yes| M[merge_lcov union DA hits]
  C -->|no / hollow| E["::error:: loud exit"]
  M --> R[CLI coverage ratchet ≥ baseline 11.00%]
```
</details>

pty-integration:
    # Issue #931 part 2: the leg was ONE job (~40 min hosted, the CI
    # critical path); it is now 3 duration-balanced shards
    # (scripts/test_integration_shards.json, file-level units). New
    # integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the cross-leg ceiling with
    # the linux leg is documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    name: PTY/CLI integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # SAME secret shape as nightly.yml's pty-integration leg and the
      # Trust model (review 2026-09-23): this is the first pull_request-time
      # leg in ci.yml that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds
      # secrets from forks, so external contributions never see them — but
      # every SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — higher-numbered — regression and would pass
      # while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks) self-skip those legs
      # gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=${{ runner.workspace }}/toolcache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # Shared-box pub-cache isolation (flake fix — run 36258687531): the
      # fa-m5 minis all share ONE user pub cache (~/.pub-cache) with every
      # concurrent job AND the box owner's local builds. A concurrent cache
      # mutation yanked image-4.10.1 sources mid-compile and exit-254'd
      # headless_tools_flag_test ("Error when reading
      # .pub-cache/.../luminance_threshold_cmd.dart") while the same
      # compile passed seconds later. Give each fa-m5 job a private cache
      # under the per-job temp root (runner-cleaned); `dart pub get` below
      # repopulates it (~1 min) and every spawned CLI sees it because the
      # PTY/headless harnesses forward PUB_CACHE explicitly. Hosted runners
      # are single-job VMs — the default cache is already private there.
      - name: Job-private pub cache (fa-m5 shared box)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "PUB_CACHE=$RUNNER_TEMP/pub-cache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # setup-python hardcodes AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY=/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache
      # on every macOS runner (hosted layout assumption) and overwrites
      # RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, so on self-hosted macs without a 'runner' user it
      # dies with "mkdir: /Users/runner: Permission denied". The only python
      # consumers here are the pure-python shard selector, the junit
      # converter and the duration-gate step below — system python3
      # (CLT on macOS, preinstalled on hosted images) suffices.
      - name: python3 available
        run: python3 --version
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

  # Issue #931 part 2: standing Linux leg. The dart-level PTY/CLI suite is
  # Linux-capable by design (ubuntu is its designed hosted fallback —
  # runner-pick below already routes the mac leg here under pool
  # saturation); it now ALSO runs on hosted arm64 IN PARALLEL with the
  # fa-m5 minis on EVERY invocation, unconditioned by path like the mac
  # leg. Motivation: 2026-09-24 the shared Mac box hit load 13-17 and
  # stretched the PTY legs to ~80 min — the hosted pool is separate
  # capacity no mini-pool saturation can starve, and a linux-only
  # regression now red-blocks the PR that caused it instead of the
  # nightly. Same suite, same shards, same --concurrency bound; NO
  # coverage: the cli-coverage ratchet stays wired to the mac-owned leg
  # (the baseline's measurement environ…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to a full commit SHA.
#
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh            # scan the repo (CI gate)
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path DIR # scan DIR/*.yml (fixtures)
#
# Exempt:
#   - ./...          first-party repo-relative actions/workflows
#   - @<40-hex>      full commit SHA (the only accepted third-party form)
# Everything else (tags, branches, latest, main, master, short SHAs) fails.

set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
# Both modes share one shape: the root's workflows (either a
# .github/workflows layout or loose *.yml/*.yaml fixtures) plus EVERY
# composite action manifest at any depth — composite action steps can
# carry remote uses: refs, so they are part of AC1's threat surface.
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
# Default (CI) mode: composite actions live under .github/actions/, OUTSIDE
# the workflows dir — root the manifest sweep at the repo root so they
# are covered (a regression here would let an unpinned remote uses: sail
# through AC1). Prune .worktrees: sibling checkouts are not this repo's
# gate surface. Fixture mode (--path) stays rooted at DIR: fixtures are
# self-contained trees.
root="$dir"
if [ "$dir" = ".github/workflows" ] && [ -d "$dir" ]; then
  root="."
fi
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  files+=("$f")
done < <(find "$root" -name .git -prune -o -path './.worktrees' -prune -o -type f \( -name 'action.yml' -o -name 'action.yaml' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no workflow files found under $dir" >&2
  exit 2
fi

violations=0
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
  refs=$(grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*uses:[[:space:]]*//') || true
  [ -n "$refs" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    [ -n "$ref" ] || continue
    case "$ref" in
      ./*) ;; # first-party repo-relative action/workflow
      docker://*)
        case "$ref" in
          *@sha256:*) ;; # digest-pinned container image
          *)
            echo "::error file=$file::unpinned container image ref: $ref"
            violations=$((violations + 1))
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *)
        sha="${ref##*@}"
        # A mutable ref whose NAME is exactly 40 chars would pass a pure
        # length glob — require hex digits (a commit SHA), nothing else.
        if [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
          : # full 40-hex commit SHA — the only accepted third-party form
        else
          echo "::error file=$file::third-party action not SHA-pinned: $ref"
          violations=$((violations + 1))
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
done

if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "check_action_pins: $violations mutable third-party action ref(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "check_action_pins: OK (all third-party actions SHA-pinned)"

## PR Description

### What changed
Unwedged `pty-coverage-gate`: the PTY legs were the only jobs still pinned to the Node-20-era `upload-artifact@ea165f8d` (v4 line) / `checkout@11d5960a` (v4), while the gate downloads with `download-artifact@3e5f45b2` (v8, strict SHA256 digest validation) — the stale uploads stopped verifying (`digest-mismatch`), the merge saw < 3 shard reports, and every run failed the hard count check. All 7 stale pins now match the repo-standard v7.0.1 SHAs used by every green leg (incl. nightly's identical suite), so all 3 shard coverage reports download and merge again and the ratchet reads the full union (≥ 11.00% baseline) instead of a partial 7.95%.

### Key decisions
- Root cause is pin drift, not #896's PUB_CACHE isolation — artifact names/paths all line up (`pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}` ↔ gate pattern ↔ `pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info`); that check is now a permanent guard.
- Baseline untouched (only-up ratchet intact); the 7.95% reading was a merge artifact of the missing/hollow shard, so no coverage-restoration issue is needed.
- New guard tests in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`: every third-party action pinned at exactly ONE full SHA repo-wide (checkout had 3, upload-artifact had 2), upload-artifact pinned to the current digest-validating line, and shard upload-name/download-pattern/count-check coherence.
- Gate hardening: a shard lcov with no `SF:` records now fails the merge loudly naming the shard, instead of silently merging a partial report the ratchet would chase.
- Drive-by: `installer-verify`/`release-provenance` checkout stragglers (v4/v5) aligned by the same one-pin invariant.

pty-integration:
    # Issue #931 part 2: the leg was ONE job (~40 min hosted, the CI
    # critical path); it is now 3 duration-balanced shards
    # (scripts/test_integration_shards.json, file-level units). New
    # integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the cross-leg ceiling with
    # the linux leg is documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    name: PTY/CLI integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # SAME secret shape as nightly.yml's pty-integration leg and the
      # Trust model (review 2026-09-23): this is the first pull_request-time
      # leg in ci.yml that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds
      # secrets from forks, so external contributions never see them — but
      # every SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — higher-numbered — regression and would pass
      # while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks) self-skip those legs
      # gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=${{ runner.workspace }}/toolcache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # Shared-box pub-cache isolation (flake fix — run 36258687531): the
      # fa-m5 minis all share ONE user pub cache (~/.pub-cache) with every
      # concurrent job AND the box owner's local builds. A concurrent cache
      # mutation yanked image-4.10.1 sources mid-compile and exit-254'd
      # headless_tools_flag_test ("Error when reading
      # .pub-cache/.../luminance_threshold_cmd.dart") while the same
      # compile passed seconds later. Give each fa-m5 job a private cache
      # under the per-job temp root (runner-cleaned); `dart pub get` below
      # repopulates it (~1 min) and every spawned CLI sees it because the
      # PTY/headless harnesses forward PUB_CACHE explicitly. Hosted runners
      # are single-job VMs — the default cache is already private there.
      - name: Job-private pub cache (fa-m5 shared box)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "PUB_CACHE=$RUNNER_TEMP/pub-cache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # setup-python hardcodes AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY=/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache
      # on every macOS runner (hosted layout assumption) and overwrites
      # RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, so on self-hosted macs without a 'runner' user it
      # dies with "mkdir: /Users/runner: Permission denied". The only python
      # consumers here are the pure-python shard selector, the junit
      # converter and the duration-gate step below — system python3
      # (CLT on macOS, preinstalled on hosted images) suffices.
      - name: python3 available
        run: python3 --version
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

  # Issue #931 part 2: standing Linux leg. The dart-level PTY/CLI suite is
  # Linux-capable by design (ubuntu is its designed hosted fallback —
  # runner-pick below already routes the mac leg here under pool
  # saturation); it now ALSO runs on hosted arm64 IN PARALLEL with the
  # fa-m5 minis on EVERY invocation, unconditioned by path like the mac
  # leg. Motivation: 2026-09-24 the shared Mac box hit load 13-17 and
  # stretched the PTY legs to ~80 min — the hosted pool is separate
  # capacity no mini-pool saturation can starve, and a linux-only
  # regression now red-blocks the PR that caused it instead of the
  # nightly. Same suite, same shards, same --concurrency bound; NO
  # coverage: the cli-coverage ratchet stays wired to the mac-owned leg
